scenes.title: Brazil
scenes.subtitle: A history told only by its sources

scenes.caption: Photo 1890
scenes.text: The Portuguese landed in the so-called "New World" on April 22, 1500, commanded by Pedro Álvares Cabral, an explorer on his way to India under the sponsorship of the Kingdom of Portugal and the support of the Catholic Church.

scenes.caption: Photo 1890
scenes.text: On September 7, 1822, prince regent Pedro declared Brazil's independence from Portugal and so the Kingdom of Brazil became the Empire of Brazil, in which he became its first emperor.

scenes.caption: Photo 1890
scenes.text: Growing political instability within the republic brought its downfall in 1930, when a military coup headed by Getúlio Vargas overthrew the republic.

scenes.caption: Photo 1890

scenes.caption: Photo 1890
scenes.text: In the 1980s, another American archaeologist, Anna Curtenius Roosevelt, led excavations and geophysical surveys of the mound Teso dos Bichos.

scenes.caption: Photo 1875
scenes.text: In 1493 the papal bull inter caetera divided claims to the New World territories between Spain and Portugal and was revised in 1494 by the Treaty of Tordesillas which moved the dividing line further west.

scenes.caption: Photo 1875
scenes.text: Forced to defend against repeated attacks by Portuguese colonial power, the warriors of Palmares were experts in capoeira, a martial arts form developed in Brazil by African slaves in the 16th century.

scenes.caption: Photo 1851
scenes.text: Since he had no direct heirs, Philip II of Spain, who was his uncle (and whose grandfather was the Portuguese King Manuel I of Portugal), was the only successor and took control of the Portuguese administration in 1580.

scenes.caption: Photo 1890

scenes.caption: Photo 1890
scenes.text: In 1815, the king vested Brazil with the dignity of a united kingdom with Portugal and the Algarves.

scenes.caption: Photo 1890
scenes.text: Brazil's independence was recognized with the Treaty of Rio de Janeiro in 1825.

scenes.caption: Photo 2025 · Salvador de Bahia
scenes.text: Tancredo Neves was elected president in an indirect election in 1985 as the nation returned to civilian rule.

scenes.caption: Photo 2025 · Salvador de Bahia
scenes.text: Fernando Collor de Mello was the first elected president by popular vote after the military regime in December 1989 defeating Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in a two-round presidential race and 35 million votes.

scenes.caption: Photo 2025 · Salvador de Bahia
scenes.text: On 1 January 2003, Lula was sworn in as the first-ever elected leftist President of Brazil.

scenes.title: What the sources leave out
scenes.text: Before 1493, history is not dated in these sources: oral traditions, archaeology and local sources are still to be brought in.
